raw:
Review of US-10-01 at 94a466b. I found one blocking defect: the Ollama check goes through an HTTP proxy when the proxy environment variables are set. The gates are green at that commit: fmt, clippy `-D warnings`, and `cargo test --workspace` (193 + 445 + 91 passed). I checked the `ureq` behaviour with a throwaway probe in /tmp, which I have deleted. The working tree is back on `main`.

BLOCKING

B1 [security] crates/core/src/ollama.rs:101-104 — `check()` builds its agent with `Agent::config_builder()` and never disables proxying.
- ureq 3.5 defaults to `proxy: Proxy::try_from_env()`, which reads `ALL_PROXY`, `HTTPS_PROXY` and `HTTP_PROXY`.
- `localhost` is exempt only if `NO_PROXY` lists it.
- Probe: with `HTTP_PROXY=http://127.0.0.1:<port>` set, a `get("http://localhost:11434/api/version")` made the probe's fake proxy see a `CONNECT` request.
- Scenario: a user on a corporate or desktop proxy starts the app with the default address. The Ollama probe goes to the proxy, which may be a remote machine, so the app sends something to a host that is neither Google nor this computer.
- This breaks criterion #4 (`MOD-10-NFR-02`, `NFR-06`). It also makes Ollama look "not available" behind a proxy that can't reach the user's localhost.
- Fix: add `.proxy(None)` to the config builder. Optionally add `.max_redirects(0)` as well (see N2). Add a test that sets `HTTP_PROXY` to a listener and asserts that listener receives nothing while the fake Ollama answers.

NON-BLOCKING

N1 crates/app/src/description.rs (test `ollama_is_asked_only_at_its_address_and_google_nothing`) — the name promises "Google nothing", but it never looks at Google or any other destination.
- It only checks that the fake Ollama's own record holds `GET /api/version` and `GET /api/tags`, plus a trivial `is_local(address)` assertion.
- It would stay green with the B1 defect, so it doesn't prove criterion #4.
- Fix: rename it, or have it record all outbound connections (for example a proxy-env listener, as in B1).

N2 crates/core/src/ollama.rs:101 — `ureq` follows up to 10 redirects by default.
- A service at the Ollama address that answers `/api/version` with a 302 to another host makes the app contact that host, which the settings warning never mentioned.
- Fix: `.max_redirects(0)`.

N3 crates/core/src/settings.rs:87-88 — `ollama_address` and `ollama_model` are loaded verbatim.
- A hand-edited `ollama_address = ` (empty) or `ollama_address = foo` gives an address that `ollama::address()` would have refused.
- The box then says "Ollama is not available at " and the settings warn that the address "leaves this computer". The same happens with an empty `ollama_model =`.
- Fix: on load, validate with `ollama::address` and `trim().is_empty()`, and fall back to the defaults.

N4 crates/core/src/ollama.rs:138-143 — `has_model` returns false when `/api/tags` answers 200 with a body that isn't JSON.
- The box then says "The model … is not installed", which is wrong; something other than Ollama is answering.
- Fix: map a parse failure to `NotRunning`.

N5 crates/core/src/ollama.rs:56-59 — `address()` accepts userinfo (`http://user:pw@host`).
- The credentials are stored in plain text in the settings file and printed in "Ollama is not available at …".
- Fix: reject URLs with a username or password, or hide them in the message.

N6 crates/app/src/main.rs (`ollama_changed`, `description.availability = Unknown`) — after any settings change the box reads as available until the next answer.
- Typing into it in that window loses nothing, but it shows as usable even when the new address is down.
- This is the documented DEC-217 trade-off, so it is only a nit.

N7 crates/app/src/main.rs, `go_to_box` — it drops every `Event::Text` of the frame, not only the `q`.
- Characters typed in the same frame as `q` are lost. This is a very small window.
- Fix: remove only the first `q` event.

N8 crates/core/src/settings.rs — there is no unit test for the new `descriptions`, `ollama_address` and `ollama_model` keys.
- The round trip is only covered indirectly by `tc_10_01`.
- Fix: add a short load/serialize test next to the existing settings tests.

N9 scripts/cargo_report.py — it doesn't trace to US-10-01. It is delivery-loop infrastructure added inside a story diff, and it is untested. It's harmless but outside the story.

N10 docs — `DECISIONS.md` DEC-216 says "no new crate enters the lock file". That holds: `Cargo.lock` only adds the `ureq` and `url` dependency edges on `calendar-core`. The decision does not mention the proxy behaviour (B1).

CRITERIA
Scenario results are listed after the numbered criteria.

#1 met — settings section, defaults and persistence (`tc_10_01`; `Settings` save/load).
#2 met — box, `q` and the shortcut-list entry are gone when off and back when on (`tc_10_02`, plus the unit test in `shortcuts.rs`).
#3 met — warning for a non-local address, none for `localhost`, `127.0.0.1` and `[::1]` (`tc_10_03`; `is_local` parses the URL, and I found no parser mismatch between `url` and `http::Uri` for backslash or `@` tricks).
#4 unmet — default-address traffic can leave this computer via a proxy from the environment (B1). TC-10-04 BLOCKED (DEC-215) is external evidence, not a finding. The substitute test (N1) doesn't prove the criterion.
#5 met on content — the README section covers the Ollama install, `ollama pull gemma4:e4b`, links to ollama.com and the library page, and says the app works without them. The read-through itself is external — MANUAL TC-10-05.

Scenarios and edge cases
- Ollama not running: met (`tc_10_06` case A).
- Model missing: met (`tc_10_06` case B).
- Ollama starts later: met (`tc_10_07` step 3).
- Ollama stops while the box is open: met via Enter or focus (`tc_10_07` steps 1-3). Step 4 is external — BLOCKED, DEC-215.
- Invalid address keeps the previous one: met (unit test and the `form.wrong_address` warning). The UI path is only partly covered by `tc_10_03`.

IMPACT: `shortcuts::command(key, descriptions)` and `shortcuts::listed(descriptions)` changed signature. `SHORTCUTS` grew to 14 entries with `q` bound to a new `Command::DescribeEvent`. The `Settings` file gains three keys, `descriptions`, `ollama_address` and `ollama_model`. `CalendarApp` gains five fields, and the side panel, the settings dialog and the shortcut handler all depend on `settings.ollama.on`. `calendar-core` now links `ureq` and `url` and exposes a `fake` feature used by the app's dev-dependencies. The main risk elsewhere is any code that assumes `q` is not a shortcut or reads the settings file strictly. The new network path is the Ollama probe in `ollama.rs`, which is why B1 matters for `NFR-06`.
